turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Is this volume all right for you?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yes, as long as you do not turn away.

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: I brought her in today. She has been uneasy about her chest.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: What can I help you with today?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I have not felt right lately, my chest is bothering me.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: What does the pain feel like?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Pardon? I did not hear you.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Sorry about that. Let me ask it another way. Can you describe the pain for me?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: It feels like a heavy weight sitting on my chest.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Does the pain spread anywhere, like your arm or jaw?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, it stays right where it is.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: When did this start?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: About three days ago, I think.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Does it come on when you are active?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, it comes even when I am sitting.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I am scared this could be a heart attack. Is that what this is?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I understand the worry. That is why we are looking at it carefully today, and we will talk about what we find.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: What have you done to get relief?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I have not taken anything for it.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Any dizziness or lightheadedness?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, I have not fainted.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Do you break out in a sweat with it?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yes, I get clammy.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Do you have trouble breathing with it?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, my breathing is fine.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Has anyone in your family had heart trouble at a young age?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: My father had a heart attack in his fifties.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Do you smoke, or have high blood pressure, diabetes or high cholesterol?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I have diabetes. I have never smoked.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Have you ever had a heart procedure, like a stent or bypass surgery?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, never.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Can you tell me your daily medicines?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I take Metformin.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Before you go, let me go over the plan. First, see the heart specialist within two weeks. Second, call 911 if the pain gets worse or does not stop. Just so I know I explained it clearly, can you tell me in your own words what you will do?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I will see the heart specialist in two weeks and call 911 if the pain gets worse or will not stop.

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: I will make sure she follows the plan.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Is there anything else you want to ask me?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, I think I understand.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Thank you for coming in. Take care.
